diagnosis.mechanism: per-frame INDEPENDENT restyling has NO temporal-coherence mechanism: every frame is re-imagined from scratch against its own source frame, so (a) inter-frame style/color variance manifests as global FLASHING (the pitch region pulsing), (b) prompt-adherence variance manifests as the tactical FLIPPING between board-like and non-board-like renders, and (c) fast goal-mouth motion manifests as HALLUCINATED EXTRA BALLS (each frame independently re-draws the ball during the deflection/save). The per-frame lane was the right fix for verdict 2's ground (style fidelity — the anime style is now approved) but per-frame independence is unpassable BY CONSTRUCTION for temporal consistency, exactly as the synthetic fixture was for event identity (verdict 1) and the filter class was for style fidelity (verdict 2). The honest pattern repeats a third time
diagnosis.consequence: the fix lane: TEMPORAL-COHERENT propagation of the approved styled frames — the reported-to-work class (the operator's copy-and-adapt directive, carried since verdict 1): optical-flow-guided video stylization coherence ('Fast Coherent Video Style Transfer via Flow Errors Reduction', MDPI; 'Coherent Online Video Style Transfer', IEEE; the Lai et al. 'Learning Blind Video Temporal Consistency' class — flow-warped blending of consecutive outputs) + the keyframe-anchored propagation class (EbSynth, ebsynth.com — 'transform videos by changing one frame'), adapted locally with OpenCV DIS flow: the SOURCE clip's own motion transports anchor styled frames forward/backward, occlusion-aware blending admits the fresh styled frames only where the warp disagrees with them, and a per-kind color harmonization pins the global tone — the ball's trajectory then follows the source's single ball, the pitch color is anchored, and each genre's style is inherited from its anchors instead of re-imagined per frame
